summary: @servicetitan/confirm-navigation ships a preinstall Bun-runtime dropper executing an obfuscated 727KB payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from a GitHub release URL, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and immediately invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-compiled script marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` whose contents are a rotated string-array plus a shift-decoder (`WV8StW`) with hex-mangled identifiers — not human-readable and unrelated to the package's advertised purpose. The advertised functionality is a small React navigation-confirmation utility whose main entry `dist/confirm-navigation.js` is roughly 8KB; fetching an alternate language runtime at install time solely to execute an opaque bundled script has no relation to that purpose. The mismatch between the well-known corporate `@servicetitan` scope and the dropper behavior is consistent with a compromised or hijacked publish. Installing this version grants install-time code execution on the installer's machine via attacker-controlled bytes hidden from Node-only inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
